# The tab-drag headers spec counts the strip before the post-drop overflow drain

## Context

Found in the first full-run receipt for the Workstation patch gate ([D#19994](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/19994#discussioncomment-19133219), [milestone v13.3.1](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/milestone/12)): `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationTabDragHeadersStayNL.spec.mjs:23`, the #19988 fix's own arm (#20005), failed at position 192 of 225 in a full `e2e/workstation` + `e2e/dashboard` run on `dev` 058e374357 (one worker): `postDropButtons.length` 2, expected ≥ 3, at line 245. The same spec passes alone on the same head (1 of 1) and passed in #20005's CI. Defect-note `ef91cb954b278e53`; root cause traced by @neo-gemini-maryam (A2A `MESSAGE:e5157d3e`), anchors verified at 058e374357.

`unowned-rationale:` a bounded spec repair any seat can take; the spec's author is a day from her budget reset; if nobody has claimed it by the time the next full gate run reports, the lead (me) takes it, because the gate needs this arm trustworthy before the cut.

## The Problem

The post-drop assertion reads the strip at the wrong boundary, and under load that boundary moves.

1. Before the drag the heavy strip is unfocused (`containsFocus === false`), so its focus-gated header actions (`showOnFocus: true`) are collapsed and three tabs fit (`stage.buttons` captured at :111–138).
2. `mousedown` on the third button (:153) focuses the strip, which reveals the contextual actions. During the drag #20005 holds the three-tab partition (`Overflow#queueSortDragProjection` queues instead of re-partitioning), so every mid-drag sample passes.
3. After `mouseup`, `SortZone#processDragEnd` (`src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:569`) clears the inline `position` first, then waits one frame (`:689`) and calls `dragEnd` (`:697`); only then does `Overflow#onSortDragEnd` drain the queued projection. `Overflow#project(false)` measures the now-visible actions, the usable extent shrinks, and `computeOverflow` keeps the two protected tabs (active + focused) and displaces the third into the menu. **That re-partition is intended** (`src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs:836–839`: "A focus change can therefore repartition the tabs; that is intended, not a regression").
4. The spec's poll (:171–184) waits only for `el.style.position === ''`, which is true at the *start* of `processDragEnd`. In a fast solo run the `page.evaluate` at :186 reads the strip inside that ~40 ms window and sees three buttons; under full-suite load the drain finishes first and the read sees the settled two. The assertion passes by timing, not by the property it names.

The retained error-context snapshot of the failed run shows the strip with three tabs and its "More tabs" control at capture time, which is the settled state a moment later: the DOM was right, the oracle's moment was wrong.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationTabDragHeadersStayNL.spec.mjs`: capture :111–138, press :153, poll :171–184, read :186–215, assertions :238–250.
- `src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:569–697` (`processDragEnd`: position clear → one frame → `dragEnd`).
- `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs:590–600` (post-drag drain), `:836–876` (extent from offered actions), `:151–168` (`computeOverflow`: active and focused tabs protected).
- `src/toolbar/Base.mjs` focus-gated actions (`showOnFocus`, #17874), the behaviour that narrows the extent on focus.
- D#19994's thesis: a passing check must carry an explicit boundary; this spec's boundary is "the drop's first frame", while its words claim "after the drop".

## The Fix

Give the post-drop read an explicit settle boundary and an oracle that does not depend on the pre-drag partition surviving focus:

- Wait for the post-drag drain, not for the inline `position` to clear: poll the Overflow plugin's state through the Neural Link (its queued-projection flag false and no projection pending) or for the rendered button set to be identical across two consecutive animation frames after `mouseup`. No fixed sleep.
- Assert the settled strip against the engine's own partition for the focused extent: the rendered buttons equal `computeOverflow`'s visible set (active + focused protected, the displaced tab present in the overflow menu), every rendered button inside the strip box with no residual inline position, and `postDropDragged.height > 16`. Keep the mid-drag `≥ 3` invariant and the `outsideFrames` check, which are #20005's purpose.
- Make the repair red-on-base deterministically: an injected pause before the read (standing in for suite load) fails the current `≥ 3` assertion on `dev` and passes the repaired oracle.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The post-drop read waits on an explicit settle signal (drain flag via NL, or two identical frames), with no fixed timeout.
- [ ] AC-2: The post-drop assertion compares the rendered set to the engine's computed partition for the focused extent, including the displaced tab in the menu; mid-drag `≥ 3`, `outsideFrames === []`, inline-position and `height > 16` checks stay.
- [ ] AC-3: With an injected pause before the read, the unrepaired spec is red on `dev` and the repaired spec is green at head (the diagonal).
- [ ] AC-4: The spec is green alone (3 of 3) and inside one full `e2e/workstation` + `e2e/dashboard` run with one worker at the fix head.

## Out of Scope

- The product behaviour: focus-revealed actions re-partitioning the strip is by design (#17874, `Overflow.mjs:836–839`); #19983 covers the hover-reveal option.
- #20017 (the warm-reload remount race), the other "passes alone, fails in the run" specimen.

## Avoided Traps

- Relaxing the count to `≥ 2`: it passes in both states and tests nothing about the drop.
- Pre-focusing the strip before capturing `stage.buttons`: with the actions revealed only two tabs fit, so the "third visible tab" the test drags no longer exists; it changes the premise instead of the boundary.
- A fixed `waitForTimeout` after the drop: the race is between two asynchronous settlements; a sleep moves the window and keeps the timing dependence.
